facts.text: Bickson, DeGennaro, Girman and Homer analysed 54 MSHA fatality reports involving off-road rigid-frame or articulated haul trucks at surface coal and metal/non-metal mines from January 2005 to June 2021 in NIOSH SME preprint 22-085, dated February 2022.
facts.quote: analysed 54 MSHA fatality reports involving off-road rigid-frame or articulated haul trucks at surface coal and metal/non-metal mines from January 2005 to June 2021 [4]

facts.text: CDC metadata records the February 2022 NIOSH haul-truck fatality conference paper, SME preprint 22-085, as not peer reviewed.
facts.quote: CDC metadata records the conference paper as not peer reviewed

facts.text: In the NIOSH analysis of 54 MSHA haul-truck fatality reports from January 2005 to June 2021, 13 deaths involved pedestrians or vehicles, 21 were berm-related, 12 were dump-point-related and eight had other causes.
facts.quote: 13 deaths involved pedestrians or vehicles, 21 were berm-related, 12 were dump-point-related and 8 had other causes.

facts.text: Among the 13 haul-truck collisions in the NIOSH analysis of January 2005–June 2021 MSHA reports, five involved light vehicles, including one double fatality, three involved pedestrians, three involved other haul trucks, and two involved other objects: a railroad car and a portable toilet.
facts.quote: Of the 13 collisions, five involved light vehicles (one a double fatality), three pedestrians, three other haul trucks and two "other" objects (a railroad car and a portable toilet).

facts.text: Of the 13 haul-truck collision incidents in the NIOSH analysis of January 2005–June 2021 MSHA reports, 12 involved a forward-moving haul truck striking a vehicle, pedestrian or related object in its forward path; the remaining incident involved a haul truck reversing into another haul truck.
facts.quote: Of these 13 incidents, 12 involved a forward-moving haul truck that collided with a vehicle, pedestrian, or related object in its forward path. The other incident involved a haul truck that reversed into another haul truck.

facts.text: Four of the 13 haul-truck collision incidents in the NIOSH analysis of January 2005–June 2021 MSHA reports involved a haul truck starting to move while victims were within 50 ft, approximately 15 m.
facts.quote: Four of the 13 involved the haul truck starting to move while the victims were within 50 ft (about 15 m).

facts.text: NIOSH judged ten of the 13 haul-truck collision incidents in its January 2005–June 2021 MSHA report analysis relevant to collision warning and avoidance systems (CXS); nine of those ten involved forward motion and one involved a reverse manoeuvre.
facts.quote: Ten of the 13 were judged relevant to collision warning and avoidance systems (CXS); nine of those ten involved forward motion and one a reverse manoeuvre.

facts.text: Among the five light-vehicle cases in the NIOSH analysis of January 2005–June 2021 haul-truck fatalities, two occurred when a stationary truck started forward, two involved a parked light vehicle in a moving truck's path, and one was a head-on interaction.
facts.quote: Among the five light-vehicle cases, two occurred when a stationary truck started forward, two when a parked light vehicle was in the path of a moving truck, and one was a head-on interaction.

facts.text: NIOSH judged one of the 13 January 2005–June 2021 haul-truck collision cases only potentially relevant to collision warning and avoidance systems because the case involved loss of control under adverse weather-related road conditions.
facts.quote: One further case was judged only potentially CXS-relevant because it involved loss of control under adverse weather-related road conditions.

facts.text: NIOSH judged two of the 13 January 2005–June 2021 haul-truck collision cases unrelated to collision warning and avoidance systems; both involved a stopped haul truck unintentionally moving or rolling forward and crushing a person on the ground.
facts.quote: The remaining two, judged unrelated to CXS, "involved a stopped haul truck that unintentionally moved or rolled forward and crushed a person on the ground".

facts.text: Two of the five light-vehicle deaths described in the NIOSH January 2005–June 2021 haul-truck analysis involved a haul truck driving over a parked pickup whose strobe light was determined to be switched off.
facts.quote: Two of the five light-vehicle deaths involved the haul truck driving over a parked pickup whose strobe light "was determined to be switched off"

facts.text: In one parked-pickup fatality in the NIOSH January 2005–June 2021 haul-truck analysis, the pickup was momentarily hidden by the haul truck's cab pillar.
facts.quote: in one of those the pickup was momentarily hidden by the haul truck's cab pillar

facts.text: In another light-vehicle case in the NIOSH January 2005–June 2021 haul-truck analysis, the light vehicle's flag was potentially impaired by inadequate illumination.
facts.quote: in another case the light vehicle's flag was "potentially impaired by a lack of adequate illumination"

facts.text: An MSHA analysis covering 2003–2017, quoted in the NIOSH haul-truck paper, found that haul-truck fatal incidents typically occurred in the frontal and operator cab areas and primarily killed light-vehicle occupants.
facts.quote: An earlier MSHA analysis (2003 to 2017), quoted in the same paper, found that for haul trucks "fatal incidents typically occurred in the frontal and operator cab areas, and the victims were primarily light vehicle occupants".

facts.text: Among 21 berm-related haul-truck deaths in the NIOSH January 2005–June 2021 analysis, loss of control accounted for nine, impairment for six, mechanical failure for three, and an absent or inadequate berm for two.
facts.quote: Among the 21 berm-related deaths, loss of control accounted for nine, impairment for six, mechanical failure for three, and an absent or inadequate berm for two.

facts.text: The NIOSH haul-truck fatality paper states that descending grades steeper than 9% at excessive speed place the retarder at a disadvantage.
facts.quote: The paper notes that descending grades steeper than 9% at excessive speed "place the retarder at a disadvantage".

facts.text: Of the 12 dump-point haul-truck deaths in the NIOSH January 2005–June 2021 analysis, six were reverse-overs and six were ground failures.
facts.quote: Of the 12 dump-point deaths, six were reverse-overs and six were ground failures

facts.text: In ten of the 12 dump-point haul-truck deaths in the NIOSH January 2005–June 2021 analysis, the berm was inadequate or absent.
facts.quote: in ten the berm was inadequate or absent

facts.text: Among the 12 dump-point haul-truck deaths in the NIOSH January 2005–June 2021 analysis, the driver was unbelted in seven cases, belted in two, and of unknown belt status in three.
facts.quote: the driver was unbelted in seven, belted in two, and unknown in three.

facts.text: In two inadequate-berm dump-point fatality cases in the NIOSH haul-truck analysis, drivers used the berm as a bump stop; repeated pounding by the rear wheels pushed the berm back until it became too close to the dump-point edge.
facts.quote: In two inadequate-berm cases drivers had been using the berm as a bump stop and "the constant pounding of the rear wheels of the haul truck pushed the berm back until it eventually became too close to the edge of the dump point".

facts.text: An analysis of 133 haul-truck-related fatalities in the USA from 1995 to 2010 found that drivers died mainly from loss of control, ground failures and two-vehicle collisions.
facts.quote: An analysis of 133 haul-truck-related fatalities (USA, 1995 to 2010) found that drivers died mainly from loss of control, ground failures and two-vehicle collisions

facts.text: An analysis of 133 haul-truck-related fatalities in the USA from 1995 to 2010 found that non-drivers died mainly from unexpected machine movement, falls from vehicles and being hit by other vehicles.
facts.quote: while non-drivers died mainly from unexpected machine movement, falls from vehicles and being hit by other vehicles [37].

facts.text: Kecojevic and Radomsky's study of loader and haul-truck fatalities from 1995 to 2002, as summarized in the NIOSH paper, found rollovers and collisions with pedestrians to be the most common accident types.
facts.quote: Kecojevic and Radomsky's study of loader and haul-truck fatalities (1995 to 2002), as summarized in the NIOSH paper, found rollovers and collisions with pedestrians to be the most common accident types

facts.text: Kecojevic and Radomsky's study of loader and haul-truck fatalities from 1995 to 2002, as summarized in the NIOSH paper, identified mechanical failure and failure to obey warning signals as the most common root causes.
facts.quote: with mechanical failure and "failure to obey warning signals" as the most common root causes [4].
